findings.title: Backup code login rejected for SAML/Google (non-CAL) users
findings.body: In the credentials authorize() flow, the guard `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode) throw new Error(ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled)` (and the similar check on line 117) runs before the new backup-code branch. When a SAML or Google user with 2FA enabled goes through the `/auth/login?totp=...` flow and submits a backup code, `credentials.totpCode` is empty (the UI explicitly clears it when switching to 'Lost access'), so authorize() throws ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled before ever reaching the backup-code verification. Backup codes therefore can never be used by non-CAL identity provider users — exactly the users most likely to need account recovery. The condition should also pass when `credentials.backupCode` is present.

findings.title: Backup code single-use guarantee is racy (read-modify-write)
findings.body: Backup code consumption decrypts the stored codes, checks indexOf, then nulls the entry and re-encrypts in a separate `prisma.user.update`. Two concurrent login requests presenting the same backup code will both read the pre-consumption state, both find the code, and both succeed before either writes back. Backup codes are documented to the user as 'can be used exactly once', but this check-then-act sequence allows parallel reuse. The consumption should be made atomic (e.g., conditional update/transaction) or the finding at least acknowledged.

findings.title: Closing the modal via X/outside click after enabling 2FA skips onEnable
findings.body: After a successful TOTP verification the flow now moves to DisplayBackupCodes, and `onEnable()` is only invoked from the explicit 'Close' button handler on that step. If the user instead dismisses the dialog via the dialog's close affordance or outside interaction (`onOpenChange`), `onEnable()` never runs and `resetState()` is never called. The parent settings page relies on onEnable to refresh the two-factor switch state, so the UI will show 2FA as disabled even though it was just enabled server-side (until a manual refresh). The backup-codes step should treat any dialog close as completion, or the parent should refresh on open change.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order
findings.body: The show/hide password button in PasswordField now has `tabIndex={-1}`, making it unreachable via keyboard navigation in every form that uses PasswordField (login, password change, 2FA setup, etc.). Keyboard and screen-reader users can no longer reveal their password to check for typos. If the intent was to fix tab order on a specific form, that should be solved locally rather than removing the control from the tab order globally.

findings.title: No test covers the actual backup-code login flow
findings.body: The PR's core feature — logging in with a backup code via 'Lost access' — has no test coverage; the file only adds a TODO comment acknowledging this. The existing tests were adjusted for the new backup-codes display step, but nothing exercises a successful backup-code login, a wrong backup code, code consumption (single use), or the third-party identity provider case where backup codes are currently broken. A login-with-backup-code e2e test would have caught the non-CAL identity provider rejection in next-auth-options.
